text: The crossing is open. I thought that meant they could finally go home. Why is no one moving? Their identities are marked invalid. Transit, food distribution, shelter access, all refused. The district recognizes their bodies but denies that they belong here. They survived the wall. Now they have to prove they exist before someone will give them water. Stay with us. We'll find another way. No chains, no prison doors, just a light that says no and a city trained to look away. The scanners aren't losing their names. Something upstream is removing them. Every rejection carries the same command signature. There's a service passage beneath the processing hall. No public entrance, no queue. That's usually where they hide the useful doors. District Identity Registry. It controls the exclusion list and holds the original records. Destroying it could erase the only evidence these people have left. Then we keep the records intact. Get inside, recover their identities, and stop the registry from locking them out again. I'll keep this queue safe. Bring their names back. All of them. Squad, move.
